I got a total of about $1,000 in bills from the hospital. Kind of a bullshit thing too. I had an annual physical as required by my work a month ago. During the physical, they found an abnormality with my EKG (they haven't the past few years). The people doing the physical said that the abnormality was probably equipment error, but that I should follow up with my primary doctor as I offered that I had been experiencing minor discomfort in my chest recently too. A couple days later I told my primary doctor about this and she recommended that I go to the ER, which I did that day. The ER doc did a battery of tests and found absolutely nothing. The doc wasn't outright chiding me for coming in but he kind of had that "WTF are you doing here" attitude. I think he was going to do fewer tests until he asked if there was a history of heart problems in my family and I started in about how both my grandpa's ate heart attacks for breakfast (I think they had 12 between the two, and this is back when heart attacks were heart attacks). Anyway, I was mildly surprised when I got a bill this week for only about $150, thinking I had dodged a financial bullet. But then today I got another bill today for about $900. I guess the first bill was from the doc himself, the second bill was from the hospital. I am doing fine financially, but $1,000 is real money to me. It's not so much the cost as the unnecessary-ness of it all. If I had kept my mouth shut during the original physical, the call to my primary doctor, or even the ER doc, I could have avoided some if not all of this BS.

Lessons learned: lie to your doctor and always, always keep your mouth shut.
